about: Prompt tuning: the starting point for every prompt. soundlab/tuning.py documents the shape; AGENTS.md says how agents use it.

alerts.note: Earcon kits: the model makes single notes, alerts.py retunes and sequences them. Recordings: whole takes.

instruments.note: Solo auditions of the music's candidate instruments, one instrument each.

music.note: A spine from text, then the other levels derived from it with audio-to-audio (music.py).

taste.text: Music: the close profile is much better than contrast (levels that keep the spine's chords, with gentler contrast).

stable-audio-3-medium.name: Stable Audio 3 Medium
stable-audio-3-medium.summary: SoundLab's engine. Trained on Freesound and AudioSparx clips and their metadata, and run at cfg 1.0 with no negative prompt, so it follows literal descriptions and the training data's tags. Under 1 s per sound-effect take; about 12 GB of VRAM.

rules.text: Be explicit and concrete, one idea per prompt: name the physical source, the action, and how it was recorded.
rules.why: At cfg 1.0 it takes the words literally; a second idea blurs into the first.

rules.text: Use the training data's tags: TrackType: SFX for sound effects; TrackType: Music, VocalType: Instrumental, Genre: …, Instruments: … for music; TrackType: Instrument for one instrument alone.
rules.why: The metadata it was trained on.

rules.text: No negations: "no music" or "without hiss" only adds the word. Say it positively (dry, close, clean).
rules.why: There's no negative prompt at cfg 1.0.

rules.text: No game lore: names like draugr or Mist-Walker mean nothing to it. Say what physically makes the sound.
No mixing-engineer adjective lists ("warm rounded attack, soft organic timbre…"): mastering handles tone, the prompt describes the sound.
rules.why: Emberhold, 2026-10-14: the project's own prompts with that tail (el) won 14% of sounds; the same descriptions without it (core) won 25%.

rules.text: Split multi-part sounds: "a body falls and a man groans" is two generations mixed, not one prompt.
Short and literal wins: about 18 words.
rules.why: Emberhold, 2026-10-14, share of sounds won: core (~18 words) 25%, tags (~17) 20%, vivid (~42) 14%, el (~36) 14%, plain (~18) 13%, alt (a different source, ~29) 9%.

rules.text: Natural recordings (animals, crowds) are used whole: chopping and retuning them sounds artificial.
Pitch and rhythm can't be prompted exactly. For a motif, ask for one single note at a time; alerts.py retunes and sequences them and checks the pitch.
Give the tempo, the mode or key, the instruments, and one mood word. For a set that must mesh, one tempo and key everywhere.

templates.sfx: TrackType: SFX, {what physically makes it} {doing what, once}, {one detail of the action}, {close mic / distant}, {indoors / outdoors}.
templates.alerts: One single {low | high} note {plucked on | bowed on | struck on} {the instrument, plainly}. One note only. {its tone, in a few words}
templates.instruments: TrackType: Instrument, VocalType: Instrumental, Genre: {genre}, Instruments: {instrument}. {what it plays, in one sentence}, {tempo} BPM, {key}, close mic, dry room.
templates.music: TrackType: Music, VocalType: Instrumental, Genre: {genre}, Genre: {genre}, Instruments: {instruments}. {mood}, {style}: {who plays what, plainly}, {tempo} BPM, {key or mode}, {meter}.

examples.prompt: TrackType: SFX, an axe striking a pine log, one crisp chop, close mic, outdoors.
examples.why: The shape to start from: source, action, recording.

examples.prompt: arrow impact, turf, ground, thock, single hit, short, solid, earthy, foley, close, clean, dry
examples.why: A Freesound-style tag caption; picked for arrow_hit.

examples.prompt: Cold wind howls and moans over bare rock on a high mountain pass at night, gusts whistling through crags and pebbles rattling.
examples.why: A plain description of what physically makes it; picked for amb_night_highlands.

examples.prompt: Two short, low calls on a wooden cow horn from the village, firm but warm and woody, a soft breathy attack, gentle outdoor air. Warm, mellow and rounded, smooth muted highs, gentle swell in and out, restrained dynamics, modest natural reverb, intimate rather than cinematic.
examples.why: The second half is a mixing-engineer tail: words, not sound.

moss-soundeffect-v2.0.name: MOSS-SoundEffect v2.0
moss-soundeffect-v2.0.summary: A 1.3B diffusion transformer for sound effects, run outside SoundLab (its own runtime) and imported into the index. It takes a negative prompt beside the prompt. About 24 s per take here, against under 1 s for Stable Audio 3.

rules.text: It takes a negative prompt: put what to avoid there, and keep the prompt itself positive.
rules.why: The imported takes carry one, e.g. "piercing peaks, hiss, metallic ringing, cinematic boom".

rules.text: Prompts written for Stable Audio 3 don't carry over. Its own style still needs finding: start from short literal captions.
rules.why: Emberhold, 2026-10-14: fed the same prompts, moss-core won 1 of 7 sounds, moss-el and moss-vivid 0 of 7; 3 of 84 takes silent.
